During 2020–2021, the percentage of U.S. adults who were in families having problems paying medical bills during the previous 12 months was 11.3%.
Non-Hispanic Black or African American adults (16.8%) were most likely to be in families having problems paying medical bills
followed by Hispanic or Latino (13.5%), non-Hispanic White (10.0%), and non-Hispanic Asian (5.7%) adults.

equity.level_reason: The outcome is a social determinant (problems paying medical bills) reported by race/ethnicity and Hispanic origin subgroup, but values are only ranked side by side with CIs; no difference or ratio is computed, so the cap at 2 applies.

level_alternative.reason: The outcome is itself an SDOH measure and the ranking (Black 16.8% vs Asian 5.7%; range 9.7% to 18.8%) could be read as a quantified contrast.
